hyps.why: Replacing a parameter-free pooling on the input edge with a 3x3 conv adds learnable capacity, giving large gains on all datasets.
Swapping an avg-pool for a conv on edge 4 consistently improves accuracy across datasets.
Replacing pooling with a learnable conv on the direct input-output edge helps.
A skip connection is a better direct edge than a blurring avg-pool, improving all three datasets.
Replacing the skip on the output edge with pooling degrades the identity path, hurting especially ImageNet16-120.
With the direct edge 3 absent, the cell relies on the skip path through edge 5, so converting it to a conv loses that benefit.
Removing edge 3 when edge 5 is already none leaves few paths to the output, causing large drops.
When the direct input-output edge is missing, an identity on edge 0 improves gradient flow into the rest of the cell.
When edge 0 is already a strong 3x3 conv, upgrading edge 2 from skip yields diminishing returns versus weaker edge 0.
Removing edge 0 hurts more when the alternative path via edge 1 is a parameter-free pool that cannot compensate.
